text:
Sam Bennett has two Stanley Cups and a Conn Smythe Trophy from Florida's runs, and he still plays right on the edge. His week included two goals in a win at Columbus on Nov. 10 and, two nights later, a fight with Detroit's Alex DeBrincat during a Panthers comeback from 4-1 down.

He has 7 goals and 11 points in 22 games at 17.4 minutes a night. The goals are honest, 7 on 6.14 expected goals (our measure of the quality of his chances), and Florida has scored 4.6 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, which has cost him points; our numbers flag him as due. The concern is volume: his chance rate is down to 0.96 expected goals per 60 minutes from 1.29 last season, and his recent ice time has dipped to about 16 minutes.

Evolving-Hockey's notes from last season show both sides. He faced top competition, 90th percentile, and created offense at even strength, but penalties cost him 2.6 goals and opponents got more chances with him on the ice than with most forwards. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him on the end of dangerous passes.
headline: Bennett is scoring, and still in the middle of everything
